project.name: Lynk 2026
project.description: An FRC (FIRST Robotics Competition) robot codebase from a different team, built on WPILib/GradleRIO (2026.2.1) with CTRE Phoenix 6, PathPlannerLib, PhotonVision, DogLog, and Lombok. Uses a LynkMotor/LynkSubsystem base-class pattern for hardware wrapping (no separate IO-interface layer) and a command-factory-style Superstructure coordinator. Kept as a read-only architectural reference under temp_reference/.

nodes.name: CalibrationTable.java
nodes.summary: Generic linear-interpolation lookup table that maps a scalar index (e.g. shot distance) to a typed setpoint by interpolating between the two nearest table entries.

nodes.name: Interpolatable.java
nodes.summary: Single-method interface that calibration setpoint types implement so CalibrationTable can interpolate between two instances.

nodes.name: LynkMotor.java
nodes.summary: Wrapper around a CTRE TalonFX motor controller that adds stall detection, a homing/zeroing command sequence, and config application on top of the raw Phoenix 6 API.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps CTRE Phoenix 6 TalonFX calls behind a reusable helper so subsystem classes avoid touching vendor APIs directly, in line with the IO-isolation pattern.

nodes.name: LynkSubsystem.java
nodes.summary: Base subsystem class every Lynk subsystem extends, centralizing motor registration and per-motor plus global current/telemetry logging in periodic().

nodes.name: Aiming.java
nodes.summary: Static utility class computing shoot-on-the-move virtual targets, hub/pass alignment tolerances, and the robot's automatic aiming rotation consumed by the shooter and drivetrain.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements an iterative shoot-on-the-move (SOTM) convergence loop (getVirtualTarget) that predicts flight time and robot movement to compute a virtual aim point.

nodes.name: Ports.java
nodes.summary: Central registry pairing CAN device IDs with CAN bus assignments, used to construct every motor and sensor port referenced throughout the robot.

nodes.name: Climber.java
nodes.summary: Singleton climber subsystem wrapping a single motor configured from ClimberConstants, extending LynkSubsystem for shared telemetry.

nodes.name: ClimberConstants.java
nodes.summary: Holds the climber's gear ratio and builds the MotorConfig used to configure the climber's Kraken X60 controller.

nodes.name: ControlsConstants.java
nodes.summary: Tiny constants file exposing the currently selected driver control mode used to switch input handling.

nodes.name: Feeder.java
nodes.summary: Singleton feeder subsystem driving floor-intake and feeder rollers, with auto-reverse jam recovery and dedicated commands for intake deployment, feeding, and reversing.

nodes.name: FeederConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines feeder/floor motor gear ratios, speeds, and auto-reverse/deploy timing constants, and builds the MotorConfig objects for the feeder and floor motors.

nodes.name: Intake.java
nodes.summary: Singleton intake subsystem controlling the intake roller with pulse, reverse, and auto-unjam behaviors driven by current-draw diagnostics in periodic().

nodes.name: IntakeConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines intake gearing, voltages, pulse timing, and stall-current-diff thresholds, and builds the intake motor's MotorConfig.

nodes.name: Shooter.java
nodes.summary: Singleton shooter subsystem managing four flywheel motors (one leader, three followers), distance-based shoot/pass setpoint lookup, spin-up timing, and SysId characterization routines.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CalibrationTable-backed lookup tables (shootingTable/passingTable) keyed by distance to interpolate target RPM and time-of-flight for shots.

nodes.name: ShooterConstants.java
nodes.summary: Defines shooter gearing and timing thresholds, holds the shooting/passing CalibrationTable data plus a distance-to-time-of-flight table, and builds flywheel and kicker MotorConfig objects.

nodes.name: CalibrationTable
nodes.summary: Immutable table of calibration points supporting linear interpolation lookup by an ordered scalar index.

nodes.name: LynkMotor
nodes.summary: Motor helper encapsulating a TalonFX plus optional stall/zeroing configuration and stall-detection debounce state.

nodes.name: LynkSubsystem
nodes.summary: Shared subsystem base tracking all registered motors for aggregate current logging and per-motor telemetry, extended by every real subsystem.

nodes.name: Aiming
nodes.summary: Aiming utility class holding pose/intake system references and the full suite of hub, virtual-hub, pass, bump, and trench targeting math.

nodes.name: Ports
nodes.summary: Value type pairing a CAN device ID with a CAN bus, used to declare every device port referenced in the robot's constants files.

nodes.name: Climber
nodes.summary: Climber subsystem class exposing a singleton instance and a single climb motor stopped on construction.

nodes.name: ClimberConstants
nodes.summary: Static holder for the climber's gear ratio and its motor configuration builder.

nodes.name: Feeder
nodes.summary: Feeder subsystem class managing floor and feeder motors, a follower relationship between the two floor motors, and a reverse-jam timer.

nodes.name: FeederConstants
nodes.summary: Static holder for feeder/floor gearing, speeds, auto-reverse/deploy timings, and motor configuration builders.

nodes.name: Intake
nodes.summary: Intake subsystem class managing the intake motor and its follower, a pulse timer, and a current-diff jam-detection timer.

nodes.name: IntakeConstants
nodes.summary: Static holder for intake gearing, voltages, pulse timing, and stall-current-diff thresholds plus the motor config builder.

nodes.name: Shooter
nodes.summary: Shooter subsystem class managing four flywheel motors, shot/spinup timers, shooter mode state, and a SysId routine.

nodes.name: ShooterConstants
nodes.summary: Static holder for shooter gearing, timing thresholds, calibration tables, and motor config builders for the flywheels and kicker.

nodes.name: lookup
nodes.summary: Searches the calibration table for the two bounding points around the given index and linearly interpolates between them.

nodes.name: stallConditions
nodes.summary: Evaluates stator current and velocity against configured thresholds to determine whether the motor is currently stalled.

nodes.name: ZeroAndWait
nodes.summary: Builds a command that starts the zeroing routine and waits for stall detection to confirm the hard stop, or logs a warning when zeroing isn't configured for this motor.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Logs the active command name and, for every registered motor, streams torque/stator/supply current, velocity, position, temperature, and stall status to DogLog.

nodes.name: getVirtualTarget
nodes.summary: Iteratively converges on a shoot-on-the-move virtual aim point by predicting robot movement during projectile flight time and re-evaluating the target until the estimate stabilizes.

nodes.name: bumpAngle
nodes.summary: Clamps a requested aiming heading to stay within a bump-guard angular range relative to the current robot rotation.

nodes.name: autoAim
nodes.summary: Chooses which aiming target (test override, trench angle, virtual hub, or passing) to publish based on intake mode, active shot state, hopper status, and field zone.

nodes.name: logAll
nodes.summary: Publishes the full set of aiming diagnostics (pass target, hub/virtual-hub angles and alignment, field side) to DogLog and SmartDashboard for tuning and debugging.

nodes.name: Climber
nodes.summary: Private constructor registering the climber motor with its ClimberConstants config and stopping it at startup.

nodes.name: getMotorConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the MotorConfig (gearing, current limits, neutral mode) used to configure the climber's Kraken X60.

nodes.name: Feeder
nodes.summary: Private constructor wiring the floor and feeder motors, configuring the second floor motor as a follower of the first, and publishing the DeployIntake command to the dashboard.

nodes.name: getFeederMotorConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the MotorConfig for the feeder roller motor, including gearing, current limits, and control constants.

nodes.name: getFloorMotorConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the MotorConfig for the floor intake motor, including gearing, current limits, and control constants.

nodes.name: Intake
nodes.summary: Private constructor wiring the intake motor and its follower, stopping both, and syncing the follower's direction to the leader.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Advances the intake pulse cycle, detects a stator/supply current-draw spike signalling a jam, auto-schedules the IntakeUnjam recovery command during teleop, and logs intake diagnostics.

nodes.name: getMotorConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the MotorConfig (gearing, current limits, neutral mode) used to configure the intake roller motor.

nodes.name: Shooter
nodes.summary: Private constructor wiring the four flywheel motors (three as followers of the leader), publishing tuning/test commands to SmartDashboard, and building the flywheel SysId characterization routine.

nodes.name: runIdle
nodes.summary: Drives the flywheels at the configured idle RPM and logs the idle start/end timestamps.

nodes.name: shoot
nodes.summary: Looks up the target RPM and time-of-flight from the passing or shooting calibration table for the given distance and mode, then commands the flywheels to that target RPM.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Tracks flywheel spin-up timing and timeout, expires the 'loaded' flag, and logs flywheel speed, mode, timers, and speed-threshold booleans for tuning.

nodes.name: getFlywheelMotorConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the MotorConfig (gearing, PID slots, current limits) used to configure the four Kraken flywheel motors.

nodes.name: getKickerMotorConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the MotorConfig used to configure the shooter's Neo 550 kicker/agitator motor.

nodes.name: Hysteresis.java
nodes.summary: Static utility implementing hysteresis (deadband) logic that maps a continuous value to one of three enum states with configurable low/high thresholds to prevent state-flapping near a boundary.

nodes.name: Hysteresis
nodes.summary: Generic hysteresis calculator holding a single static `calculate` method used to debounce threshold-based zone/state transitions (e.g. field zones, trench status) in Pose.java.

nodes.name: calculate
nodes.summary: Compares a value against a threshold with a hysteresis band and returns the appropriate enum constant (current/low/high), avoiding rapid toggling when the value hovers near the threshold.

nodes.name: LoggedCommand.java
nodes.summary: Thin WPILib Command subclass that automatically logs command start/finish events via LoggedCommands, meant to be extended by commands that want built-in telemetry.

nodes.name: LoggedCommand
nodes.summary: Base Command class that hooks `initialize`/`end` to call LoggedCommands' logging helpers, giving any subclass automatic DogLog telemetry without extra boilerplate.

nodes.name: LoggedCommands.java
nodes.summary: Central factory of WPILib Commands.* wrappers (runOnce, sequence, parallel, waitUntil, etc.) that automatically attach start/finish DogLog telemetry to every command created through it, standardizing logging across the robot codebase.
nodes.languageNotes: Every factory method funnels through a single private `loggedCommand` helper that wraps a Command in a WrapperCommand; the private constructor throws to enforce the class is static-only.

nodes.name: LoggedCommands
nodes.summary: Static-only utility class exposing logged equivalents of nearly all edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Commands factory methods, ensuring every command built through it reports init/finish telemetry via DogLog.

nodes.name: loggedCommand
nodes.summary: Wraps an arbitrary Command in a WrapperCommand that logs initialize/end events through DogLog, forming the core building block every other logging factory method in this class delegates to.

nodes.name: AimOnly.java
nodes.summary: Command that rotates the swerve drivetrain in place to face a supplied auto-aim target angle without translating, using SwerveAlign's PID for rotational speed.

nodes.name: AimOnly
nodes.summary: Command implementation for a pure rotational aim-and-hold behavior driven by an autoAimSupplier optional-angle supplier, used when the robot needs to aim without translating (e.g. during autonomous shooting setups).

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Each scheduler tick, pulls the current aim target from the supplier, feeds it into SwerveAlign to compute rotational speed, and commands the swerve subsystem to rotate in place toward that heading.

nodes.name: TeleopSwerve.java
nodes.summary: Primary driver-controlled swerve command translating joystick inputs into field/robot-relative chassis motion, with support for slow mode, PacMan-style field wraparound, auto-aim override, and shooter-load speed limiting.

nodes.name: TeleopSwerve
nodes.summary: The default teleop drive command that reads driver joystick suppliers, applies deadbands/sensitivity curves, and either drives normally or hands off rotational control to auto-aim/SwerveAlign depending on active Options flags.

nodes.name: TeleopSwerve
nodes.summary: Constructs the teleop drive command from translation/strafe/rotation/speed-limit suppliers and registers the swerve subsystem as a command requirement.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Core per-tick teleop control loop that shapes stick inputs, optionally applies slow-mode/PacMan wraparound/hold-angle logic, blends in auto-aim rotation via SwerveAlign when active, and issues the final field-relative drive command to the Swerve subsystem.

nodes.name: PIDSwerve.java
nodes.summary: Command that drives the swerve chassis to a target field pose using independent X/Y PID controllers, with configurable precision tolerance and optional alliance-relative pose flipping.

nodes.name: PIDSwerve
nodes.summary: PID-based point-to-point swerve driving command used both in teleop test bindings and autos, holding separate X and Y PIDControllers plus SwerveAlign for rotation, with an isAligned/isFinished completion check gated by tolerance and an optional vision-difference sanity check.

nodes.name: PIDSwerve
nodes.summary: Builds the X/Y PIDControllers from target pose coordinates (converted to inches), configures integrator zones/ranges and tolerance bands based on the `precise` flag, and optionally flips the target pose for the red alliance.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Resets both PID controllers, arms SwerveAlign's rotational target/error tracking to the target pose's rotation, and logs the target pose at command start.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Computes X/Y PID outputs against the current estimated pose (in inches, clamped and sign-preserved), retrieves rotational speed from SwerveAlign, logs extensive telemetry, and drives the swerve subsystem toward the target.

nodes.name: SwerveToObject.java
nodes.summary: Vision/object-detection-driven command that rotates toward and drives at a detected game piece using pitch/yaw from Detection, locking onto the object's last known field position once it's momentarily lost from view.

nodes.name: SwerveToObject
nodes.summary: Command combining a rotation PID (continuous-input, driven by detected-object yaw) with a pitch-derived forward speed to chase a detected game piece, falling back to a locked last-seen field position when the object briefly drops out of view.

nodes.name: locationToSpeed
nodes.summary: Converts a detected object's pitch/yaw angles into a forward drive speed, ramping down as the object nears the bottom of frame (close range) with a small dead zone near center.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Each tick, reads the most recent detected object (or falls back to a locked field-relative position when none is visible), computes rotation via PID and forward speed via locationToSpeed, and drives the robot relative to itself toward the target.

nodes.name: Controls.java
nodes.summary: Singleton subsystem that owns the driver Xbox controller and wires every button/trigger/POV binding to swerve, shooter, feeder, intake, superstructure, and diagnostic (SysId) commands -- the central input-to-command switchboard for the robot.

nodes.name: Controls
nodes.summary: Singleton (instance) holding the driver CommandXboxController and all configureButtonBindings wiring; also exposes rumble-feedback helpers and a default TeleOpSwerve command factory bound as the swerve subsystem's default command.

nodes.name: Controls
nodes.summary: Constructs the driver controller, publishes SmartDashboard test-mode speed-limit entries, registers manual swerve coast/brake/align SmartDashboard buttons, and calls configureButtonBindings.

nodes.name: Rumble
nodes.summary: Builds a timed rumble-feedback command that pulses the driver controller's rumble motors for a duration then clears them, used to alert the driver of state changes.

nodes.name: configureButtonBindings
nodes.summary: Massive binding table mapping every driver button/bumper/trigger/POV to a command -- SysId characterization routines (swerve steer/drive, shooter), superstructure intake/shoot/pass/unjam actions, feeder/intake manual overrides, pose-reset autonomous test paths, and error/warning alerts -- the primary place where "what does this button do" is answered.

nodes.name: TeleOpSwerve
nodes.summary: Factory method that builds the default TeleopSwerve command from the driver's translation/strafe/rotation stick getters, used as the Swerve subsystem's default command.

nodes.name: Detection.java
nodes.summary: Vision subsystem that reads a PhotonVision-style camera's detected-object results, filters to the highest-confidence target with plausible pitch/yaw, and exposes helper commands/queries for other commands (e.g. SwerveToObject) to consume.

nodes.name: Detection
nodes.summary: Singleton subsystem wrapping a camera's object-detection pipeline; tracks the most recent valid detection with a timestamp so consumers can check haveRecentObject/getRecentObject or block via WaitForObject/StopUntilObject.

nodes.name: processCamera
nodes.summary: Pulls all unread camera results, filters detected objects to those within a plausible pitch/yaw window, and keeps the highest-confidence candidate as the new 'recent object' with its capture timestamp.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Runs object detection processing only outside autonomous, and logs camera connectivity, latest pitch/yaw/confidence, and recency telemetry via DogLog every cycle.

nodes.name: Pose.java
nodes.summary: Singleton subsystem owning the Pigeon2 gyro and SwerveDrivePoseEstimator; fuses odometry and vision, configures PathPlanner's AutoBuilder, and derives higher-level field-relative concepts (hub distance/bearing, alliance-flipped zones, trench-crossing status, level/tilt detection) consumed throughout autos and aiming.

nodes.name: Pose
nodes.summary: Central pose-estimation subsystem: wraps the Pigeon2 IMU and SwerveDrivePoseEstimator, wires PathPlanner's AutoBuilder/logging callbacks, and provides alliance-aware geometry helpers (flipIfRed, hubDistance/passDistance, bearing) plus hysteresis-debounced zone/trench-status classification used by autos and Aiming.

nodes.name: Pose
nodes.summary: Initializes the Pigeon2 gyro's mount pose, builds the SwerveDrivePoseEstimator seeded from current module positions, wires Vision's pose-estimator/heading-provider callbacks, and configures PathPlanner's AutoBuilder (holonomic PID controllers, robot-relative auto-drive, and path/pose logging callbacks).

nodes.name: getTrenchStatus
nodes.summary: Classifies the robot's alliance-relative trench-crossing state (e.g. entering/inside/exiting) from its blue-origin position using multiple Hysteresis.calculate checks along the trench's entry/exit boundaries to avoid flicker.

nodes.name: getZone
nodes.summary: Determines which field zone (e.g. own/opponent/neutral) a blue-origin position falls into using hysteresis-debounced X-coordinate thresholds.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Every cycle, updates the pose estimator from gyro yaw and module positions, publishes the fused pose to the field2d widget and dashboard, re-syncs pose translation from a trusted vision source when the drivetrain is disabled, and recomputes/logs field side, zone, and trench status along with hub distance/heading telemetry.

nodes.name: Swerve.java
nodes.summary: Singleton swerve drivetrain subsystem owning the four SwerveModule instances; exposes field/robot-relative drive methods, brake/coast control, an X-lock stance, SysId characterization routines for both drive and steer motors, and per-cycle telemetry.

nodes.name: Swerve
nodes.summary: The drivetrain subsystem coordinating four SwerveModules: converts field-relative or robot-relative chassis speed requests into per-module states via SwerveConstants.swerveKinematics, provides coast/brake and X-lock utilities, and runs SysId quasistatic/dynamic routines for both translation and steer characterization.

nodes.name: Swerve
nodes.summary: Instantiates the four SwerveModules, publishes SmartDashboard test buttons for CANcoder resync and a scripted forward/stop self-test sequence.

nodes.name: drive
nodes.summary: Public drive entry point that converts a translation/rotation request into field-relative chassis speeds (using the current pose heading) and delegates to driveRobotRelative.

nodes.name: driveRobotRelative
nodes.summary: Discretizes the desired chassis speeds, converts robot-relative speeds using current heading, runs them through swerve kinematics into per-module states, desaturates wheel speeds against max speed, and commands each SwerveModule to its desired state.

nodes.name: xSwerve
nodes.summary: Points each swerve module's wheel diagonally inward/outward (an X pattern) at zero drive speed to lock the chassis in place and resist being pushed.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Logs the active command name, each module's raw CANcoder angle, per-module alignment error/status, and current swerve module states every scheduler cycle.

nodes.name: SwerveAlign.java
nodes.summary: Static rotation-alignment utility built around a single shared PIDController that computes turning speed toward a target heading (with a static feedforward term) and reports whether the drivetrain is currently aligned within tolerance.

nodes.name: SwerveAlign
nodes.summary: Static-only helper wrapping a rotation PIDController (with configurable static feedforward rotationKS and max output rotationMax) used by AimOnly, TeleopSwerve, and PIDSwerve to converge the chassis heading onto a target angle.

nodes.name: getSpeed
nodes.summary: Runs the rotation PIDController against the current heading error, applies a signed static-feedforward term on top of the PID output, clamps to rotationMax, and logs PID error/derivative/output telemetry.

nodes.name: CANdleGroup.java
nodes.summary: Utility wrapper that groups multiple CTRE CANdle LED controller instances so a single logical operation (config apply, animation, solid color) can be broadcast to all of them at once.

nodes.name: CANdleGroup
nodes.summary: Holds a list of CANdle hardware instances and exposes group-wide configuration, animation, and static/RGBW color-setting operations, logging each action via DogLog.

nodes.name: applyConfigs
nodes.summary: Applies a shared CANdleConfiguration object to every CANdle in the group via each device's configurator.

nodes.name: LoggedAlert.java
nodes.summary: Static helper class providing Error/Warning/Info alert methods that simultaneously push an Elastic dashboard notification and log a DogLog fault for a given subsystem.

nodes.name: LoggedAlert
nodes.summary: Groups the three alert-severity helper methods (Error, Warning, Info) that combine Elastic notifications with DogLog fault logging for consistent operator-facing and log-based diagnostics.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Sends an error-severity Elastic dashboard notification and records a DogLog fault combining subsystem, title, and message.

nodes.name: Warning
nodes.summary: Sends a warning-severity Elastic dashboard notification and records a DogLog fault combining subsystem, title, and message.

nodes.name: Info
nodes.summary: Sends an info-severity Elastic dashboard notification and records a DogLog fault combining subsystem, title, and message.

nodes.name: Constants.java
nodes.summary: Central static constants holder for driver-station/dashboard flags, joystick sensitivity and deadband tuning, mechanism slowdown/timing values, and alert warning/error time thresholds shared across the robot code.

nodes.name: Field.java
nodes.summary: Defines static field geometry constants -- overall dimensions, pass-target zones, wall-proximity thresholds with hysteresis, and trench run lengths -- used for autonomous zone detection and pose sanity checks.

nodes.name: Shift.java
nodes.summary: Defines the Shift enum modeling sequential match-time periods with per-shift activation conditions, remaining-time calculations, and autonomous-outcome-aware active-shift lookup, driving LED/dashboard shift indicators.

nodes.name: Shift
nodes.summary: Enum of match-time shifts, each carrying a name, a time-based activation condition, and a remaining-time function; provides lookup-by-time, sequencing (next), auto-win detection, and dashboard reporting.

nodes.name: lookup
nodes.summary: Iterates all Shift enum values and returns the first whose condition function matches the given match time, throwing if none matches.

nodes.name: timeLeft
nodes.summary: Computes the time remaining in this shift for a given match time via the shift's configured time-left function.

nodes.name: wonAuto
nodes.summary: Determines which alliance won the autonomous period by parsing the FMS game-specific message and cross-referencing against the robot's own alliance color, returning an Optional<Boolean>.

nodes.name: isActive
nodes.summary: Evaluates whether this shift is currently active, accounting for shift variants whose activation additionally depends on which alliance won autonomous.

nodes.name: disabledNext
nodes.summary: Returns the next shift to become active while the robot is disabled, used to preview the upcoming match phase.

nodes.name: isNextActive
nodes.summary: Reports whether the shift following this one is currently active, used for early shift-change warnings.

nodes.name: Autos.java
nodes.summary: Singleton autonomous command builder integrating PathPlanner's AutoBuilder -- dynamically constructs scoring/intake auto sequences from dashboard chooser selections, provides path-shortening/slowing modifiers and mirroring, and tracks autonomous pose-drift error on the dashboard each periodic cycle.

nodes.name: Autos
nodes.summary: Singleton coordinating PathPlanner auto-chooser construction, named-command registration, dynamic/mirrored path following, and a suite of path-modifier helpers (shortening, slowing) used to compose full autonomous routines from dashboard-selected options.

nodes.name: Autos
nodes.summary: Builds the AutoBuilder chooser, seeds it with a 'do nothing' plus dashboard-configurable auto options, and wires a starting-pose-assumption command triggered from the dashboard.

nodes.name: DynamicPath
nodes.summary: Builds an on-the-fly PathPlannerPath from a list of poses (prefixed with the current robot pose, flipped for red alliance) and returns a command that follows it, optionally mirroring a specified auto's path.

nodes.name: deliverHopper
nodes.summary: Composes a timed command sequence that forces a vision pose update, waits for a stable pose lock, then runs the Superstructure's DeliverToHub scoring sequence, falling back to aim-only if not aligned before timeout.

nodes.name: shortenFuelPath
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a PathPlannerPath with its final waypoint pulled back toward the previous one, used to shorten the end of a fuel-collection path while preserving rotation targets and constraints.

nodes.name: shortenStartPosition
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a PathPlannerPath with its first waypoint pulled forward toward the second, used to shorten the starting segment of a path while preserving the rest of the path's configuration.

nodes.name: slowFuelIntake
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a path's final constraint zone with reduced acceleration/angular limits so the robot intakes fuel more slowly near the end of the path.

nodes.name: slowSweep
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a path's final constraint zone with reduced acceleration/angular limits to slow the robot during a sweeping fuel-collection maneuver.

nodes.name: Recover
nodes.summary: Builds a recovery auto sequence that drives back along a path while intaking and idling the shooter, then stops and delivers to the hub, used to recover from an interrupted or failed autonomous routine.

nodes.name: buildAuto
nodes.summary: Assembles a full named autonomous routine (start position, pass depth, fuel intake depth, sweep, return method) from an AutoBuilderConfig by chaining PathCommand segments with intake/shooter/feeder coordination between each leg.

nodes.name: buildAutos
nodes.summary: Constructs a family of related named autonomous routines by varying start position and priority combinations, registering each with the auto chooser and warming up the PathPlanner follower command.

nodes.name: PathCommand
nodes.summary: Loads a named PathPlannerPath file, applies an optional path modifier, and returns a command that follows either the original or the alliance-mirrored path depending on current alliance, falling back to an error-logged no-op on load failure.

nodes.name: createAutoOption
nodes.summary: Builds a SendableChooser dashboard widget populated with all values of a given enum class, registers it under a named auto-builder chooser key, and publishes it to SmartDashboard.

nodes.name: createAutoOptions
nodes.summary: Creates the full set of dashboard choosers (starting point, priorities, pass/intake depth, sweep type/speed, return method) used to configure dynamically-built autonomous routines.

nodes.name: getAutoBuilderConfig
nodes.summary: Reads the current selections from all auto-builder dashboard choosers and assembles them into an AutoBuilderConfig record.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Each cycle, rebuilds the dashboard-driven auto command when its configuration changes, and while enabled, publishes pose-drift telemetry (position/rotation error from the recorded starting pose) to the dashboard.

nodes.name: LED.java
nodes.summary: Singleton LED subsystem driving CANdle-connected strips -- exposes color/animation setters and alert-severity triggers, and periodically arbitrates between service-mode, disabled-blink, shift-warning, intake, and shot-status animations.

nodes.name: LED
nodes.summary: Singleton wrapping a CANdleGroup to provide color/animation control plus a periodic state machine that layers shift-warning, error/info/warning temp-states, and intake/shot-status indication on top of a default ready animation.

nodes.name: LED
nodes.summary: Constructs the CANdleGroup and CANdle hardware handles, sets an initial ready color, and wires a dashboard color chooser plus test-color-apply/clear buttons for manual LED debugging.

nodes.name: triggerShiftWarning
nodes.summary: Restarts the temporary-state timer to begin displaying the shift-ending warning color/animation for a configured duration.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Each cycle, selects and applies the appropriate LED animation/color by priority -- disabled service-mode override, temp alert states (error/warning/info/shift-warning) with blink timing, then intake/shot-status indication, falling back to a default ready animation.

nodes.name: LEDConstants.java
nodes.summary: Static constants for the LED subsystem: strip start index/length/brightness, CANdle animation presets for ready/service-mode/intake states, and blink-rate/temp-state/shift-countdown timing thresholds.

nodes.name: Vision.java
nodes.summary: Singleton vision subsystem wrapping PhotonVision cameras and AprilTag multi-tag pose estimation -- filters unreasonable or off-alliance-tag pose results and periodically feeds accepted vision measurements into the pose estimator with camera-mode-dependent standard deviations.

nodes.name: Vision
nodes.summary: Singleton managing one or more PhotonVision cameras, computing multi-tag pose estimates per camera, filtering by field bounds and alliance-tag presence, and periodically publishing accepted vision measurements to the robot's pose estimator.

nodes.name: poseIsReasonable
nodes.summary: Sanity-checks a candidate 3D vision pose against field boundaries and a small out-of-plane Z tolerance, rejecting results that are physically implausible.

nodes.name: processCamera
nodes.summary: Pulls all unread PhotonVision pipeline results for a given camera, computes the multi-tag field-relative robot pose for each result, and returns a list of pose/timestamp/ambiguity results for later filtering and fusion.

nodes.name: hasAllianceTag
nodes.summary: Checks whether any of the given fiducial IDs corresponds to an AprilTag belonging to the robot's own alliance, used to reject vision updates anchored on opposing-alliance tags.

nodes.name: takeSnapshot
nodes.summary: Triggers a one-shot capture/logging of the current camera view, used by scoring sequences to record evidence at the moment of a shot.

nodes.name: ForceVisionUpdate
nodes.summary: Returns a command that forces an immediate vision-based pose correction, used by autonomous routines before committing to a shot.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Each cycle, processes results from all cameras, filters out unreasonable or non-alliance-tag poses, and fuses accepted results into the pose estimator with per-camera-mode standard deviations, publishing vision telemetry and a dashboard field overlay.

nodes.name: Superstructure.java
nodes.summary: Singleton Superstructure composing shooter, intake, feeder, and vision subsystems into higher-level scoring commands (DeliverToHub, Pass, FixedDelivery, SmartShoot, Unjam) and periodically tracking match-shift timing to drive dashboard telemetry, driver rumble, and LED shift warnings.

nodes.name: Superstructure
nodes.summary: Singleton coordinator that builds composite shoot/pass/intake/unjam commands from the Shooter, Intake, Feeder, and Vision subsystems, exposes a dashboard shot-type selector, and runs a periodic loop tracking current match shift and issuing shift-ending warnings.

nodes.name: Superstructure
nodes.summary: Builds the dashboard shot-selector chooser populated from the ShotConfig enum and publishes it to SmartDashboard.

nodes.name: DeliverToHub
nodes.summary: Composes the full hub-scoring sequence: shoots, pulses intake, snapshots vision, optionally waits for aim alignment, adjusts the shot for current load, then feeds once ready -- with a timeout fallback if alignment never resolves.

nodes.name: Pass
nodes.summary: Composes a passing-shot sequence: spins up the pass shot, pulses intake, waits for pass-alignment, adjusts for load, then feeds.

nodes.name: FixedDelivery
nodes.summary: Composes a fixed (non-vision-aimed) shot sequence: spins up a deferred fixed-shot RPM based on current shooter state, pulses intake, waits for shooter readiness, adjusts for load, then feeds.

nodes.name: SmartShoot
nodes.summary: Chooses between Pass and DeliverToHub/FixedDelivery based on the dashboard-selected shot type and the robot's current field zone, dispatching to the appropriate composed scoring command.

nodes.name: periodic
nodes.summary: Each cycle, logs the active shot selection and hopper-full state, updates the current match shift from the driver-station match time, and -- once per shift transition -- schedules a driver rumble and LED shift-warning when the next shift is about to become active.

nodes.name: COTSTalonFXSwerveConstants.java
nodes.summary: Library of common commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) swerve module specs (WCP SwerveX variants, SDS MK5n, etc.), providing per-vendor wheel diameter, gear ratios, motor inverts, and CANcoder direction as static factory methods for Falcon 500 / Kraken X60 / Kraken X60 X44 motor options.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses nested static final classes per vendor/module family (WCP.SwerveXStandard, SDS.MK5n, etc.) each exposing static factory methods that return an immutable COTSTalonFXSwerveConstants instance -- a classic Team 364-style swerve constants catalog reused widely across FRC teams.

nodes.name: COTSTalonFXSwerveConstants
nodes.summary: Immutable value class holding wheel diameter/circumference, gear ratios, angle-motor PID gains, and motor/encoder inversion settings for a specific swerve module hardware configuration.

nodes.name: SwerveModuleConstants.java
nodes.summary: Small immutable record-like class bundling a single swerve module's per-module identity: drive motor ID, angle motor ID, CANcoder ID, CAN bus name, and absolute angle offset.

nodes.name: SwerveModuleConstants
nodes.summary: Plain data container for one swerve module's CAN IDs, bus assignment, and CANcoder angle offset, constructed once per module in SwerveConstants.

nodes.name: CTREConfigs.java
nodes.summary: Builds the shared Phoenix 6 TalonFXConfiguration objects (swerve angle motor, swerve drive motor) and CANcoder configuration by reading gains, current limits, inverts, and ramp rates out of SwerveConstants, so every swerve module applies identical hardware config.
nodes.languageNotes: Centralizes all CTRE Phoenix 6 config-object construction in one place, keeping vendor API calls out of the SwerveModule class per this project's hardware-isolation convention.

nodes.name: CTREConfigs
nodes.summary: Constructs and populates the three shared Phoenix 6 configuration objects (swerve angle TalonFX, swerve drive TalonFX, CANcoder) from SwerveConstants values, applied uniformly to every swerve module at init.

nodes.name: AutoConstants.java
nodes.summary: Autonomous-mode tuning constants (setup position/heading error tolerances, quick-shoot timing, path-shortening offset, slow intake/sweep velocity caps, vision wait time) plus the AutoBuilderConfig record of enums describing auto routine variants, and the PathPlanner RobotConfig built from SwerveConstants and DCMotor specs.
nodes.languageNotes: Bundles an inner record (AutoBuilderConfig) with several nested enums to describe parameterized auto-routine choices (starting point, priority, pass depth, etc.), alongside a PathPlanner RobotConfig construction with a noted TODO that it 'doesn't work' as expected.

nodes.name: AutoConstants
nodes.summary: Static holder for autonomous tuning tolerances/timings and the PathPlanner RobotConfig (mass, MOI, module config, module offsets) derived from SwerveConstants.

nodes.name: PIDSwerveConstants.java
nodes.summary: Tuning constants for PID-driven swerve alignment commands: translation/rotation PID gains (fine and rough tolerance tiers), position tolerances, iZone, max angular velocity, and object-seeking parameters used to lock onto and drive toward a detected game-piece or field target.

nodes.name: PIDSwerveConstants
nodes.summary: Static holder of PID gains and tolerances consumed by the PIDSwerve and SwerveToObject commands for closed-loop position/rotation alignment and object-seeking behavior.

nodes.name: SwerveConstants.java
nodes.summary: Central swerve drivetrain configuration: selects the physical module hardware (chosenModule from COTSTalonFXSwerveConstants), defines track width/wheelbase/kinematics/rotation center, gear ratios, motor inverts, current limits, PID/feedforward gains for angle and drive motors, max speed/angular velocity, and neutral modes -- the single source of truth every swerve-related file reads from.
nodes.languageNotes: Acts as the project's swerve 'god constants' file, deriving many values (gear ratios, motor inverts, wheel circumference) directly from the chosenModule COTS spec rather than duplicating them, so changing chosenModule cascades correctly through dependent constants.

nodes.name: SwerveConstants
nodes.summary: Static constants class defining the full swerve drivetrain configuration -- kinematics, module hardware selection, gear ratios, current limits, PID/FF gains, and speed limits -- consumed by CTREConfigs, Swerve, SwerveModule, and the swerve-related commands.

nodes.name: Conversions.java
nodes.summary: Static math helper converting between wheel rotations/RPS and linear meters/MPS given a wheel circumference, used by swerve module velocity and odometry calculations.

nodes.name: RPSToMPS
nodes.summary: Converts wheel rotations-per-second to linear meters-per-second using wheel circumference.

nodes.name: MPSToRPS
nodes.summary: Converts linear meters-per-second to wheel rotations-per-second using wheel circumference.

nodes.name: rotationsToMeters
nodes.summary: Converts a wheel rotation count into a linear meters traveled value using wheel circumference.

nodes.name: metersToRotations
nodes.summary: Converts a linear meters traveled value into a wheel rotation count using wheel circumference.

nodes.name: Elastic.java
nodes.summary: Utility for sending Elastic-dashboard notifications and programmatically switching dashboard tabs over NetworkTables, plus a builder-style Notification class for constructing dashboard alerts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a fluent/builder pattern (withTitle, withDescription, withDisplaySeconds, etc.) on an inner Notification class to construct dashboard alerts, then serializes them to JSON via Jackson's ObjectMapper for publishing over NetworkTables.

nodes.name: sendNotification
nodes.summary: Serializes a Notification object to JSON and publishes it to the Elastic dashboard's NetworkTables topic.

nodes.name: Elastic
nodes.summary: Static utility class exposing notification-sending and tab-selection helpers for the Elastic dashboard, plus a nested Notification builder for constructing dashboard alert payloads.

nodes.name: SwerveModule.java
nodes.summary: Represents a single swerve drive module, directly wrapping CTRE Phoenix 6 TalonFX drive/angle motors and a CANcoder to expose setDesiredState, module state/position, and coast/brake mode controls.
nodes.languageNotes: Directly instantiates and configures CTRE Phoenix 6 TalonFX/CANcoder hardware inline rather than behind an IO interface — a hardware-coupled pattern our project's architecture rules explicitly forbid outside IOReal implementations and the sanctioned CommandSwerveDrivetrain exception.

nodes.name: SwerveModule
nodes.summary: Constructor that configures the module's CANcoder and TalonFX angle/drive motors from SwerveModuleConstants and resets the angle motor to the CANcoder's absolute position.

nodes.name: setSpeed
nodes.summary: Drives the module's drive motor open-loop (duty cycle) or closed-loop (velocity voltage) based on the desired swerve module state.

nodes.name: resetToAbsolute
nodes.summary: Re-seeds the angle motor's internal position from the CANcoder's absolute reading, with a settling delay for CAN latency.

nodes.name: getState
nodes.summary: Returns the module's current SwerveModuleState (velocity and angle) computed from motor telemetry via Conversions.RPSToMPS.

nodes.name: getPosition
nodes.summary: Returns the module's current SwerveModulePosition (distance and angle) used for swerve odometry.

nodes.name: SwerveModule
nodes.summary: Hardware-coupled swerve module class wrapping a TalonFX drive motor, TalonFX angle motor, and CANcoder, providing state control, telemetry, alignment checking, and neutral mode switching.

nodes.name: Robot.java
nodes.summary: TimedRobot entry point that wires up DogLog telemetry, WebServer, subsystem singletons, and the CommandScheduler, and dispatches robotInit/periodic/mode-transition callbacks across disabled, autonomous, teleop, and test modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends WPILib's TimedRobot and centralizes cross-cutting startup concerns (logging config, dashboard buttons for power-rail/signal-logger toggles, subsystem instantiation order) rather than delegating them to a separate RobotContainer.

nodes.name: robotInit
nodes.summary: Performs one-time startup: sets brownout voltage, starts the deploy-directory WebServer, configures DogLog options, logs build metadata from the deploy version file, instantiates subsystem singletons, wires button bindings, and registers dashboard toggle buttons for the 5V rail and signal logging.

nodes.name: robotPeriodic
nodes.summary: Runs every loop cycle to elevate thread priority, drive the CommandScheduler, log loop-overrun and error/warning status, and update match-time and shift-status dashboard values.

nodes.name: autonomousInit
nodes.summary: Cancels any leftover default swerve command, fetches the selected autonomous command from Autos, schedules it, and switches the Elastic dashboard to the autonomous tab.

nodes.name: teleopInit
nodes.summary: Cancels the autonomous command, stops and brakes the swerve drivetrain, installs the teleop swerve default command, and switches the Elastic dashboard to the teleop tab.

nodes.name: isRed
nodes.summary: Reads the DriverStation alliance color and returns whether the robot is on the red alliance, logging the result.

nodes.name: Robot
nodes.summary: Main WPILib TimedRobot subclass that boots logging/dashboard infrastructure, owns CTRE config and Field2d instances, and dispatches robot lifecycle callbacks across all competition modes.

nodes.name: WPILib-License.md
nodes.summary: BSD-style license text from FIRST and other WPILib contributors, covering redistribution and use terms for the WPILib libraries bundled with this robot project.

nodes.name: build.gradle
nodes.summary: Gradle build configuration for the FRC robot project: wires up the GradleRIO and Lombok plugins on a Java 17 toolchain, defines the RoboRIO deploy target/artifacts, declares WPILib and vendor dependencies (including JUnit 5 test wiring), and registers a custom writeGitInfo task that stamps a `git describe` version string into the deploy directory on every build.
nodes.languageNotes: The custom `writeGitInfo` task shells out via `exec { commandLine 'git', 'describe', ... }` and only rewrites version.txt when the hash actually changed, preserving the file's mtime so the jar task's up-to-date check isn't needlessly invalidated on every build.

nodes.name: gradlew.bat
nodes.summary: Standard Gradle wrapper batch script for Windows that resolves a Java runtime via JAVA_HOME (or PATH) and launches org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain with the wrapper jar on the classpath.
nodes.languageNotes: Unmodified stock Gradle wrapper script (Apache-2.0, auto-generated by Gradle) rather than custom project logic; its :findJavaFromJavaHome/:execute/:fail labels are boilerplate control-flow jumps, not project-specific routines.

nodes.name: settings.gradle
nodes.summary: Gradle settings file that configures plugin management to resolve the WPILib 2026 Maven repository from the OS-specific WPILib "public" home folder (Windows vs. Unix paths), plus a system property workaround to ignore unresolved native-header dependencies.

nodes.name: DogLog.json

nodes.name: PathplannerLib.json

nodes.name: Phoenix6-frc2026-latest.json

nodes.languageNotes: Largest vendordep in the project (449 lines) because it enumerates per-platform JNI and C++ binary artifacts (windows/linux/osx/athena/arm variants) alongside the Java dependency — typical of CTRE's multi-platform simulation + roboRIO deployment support.

nodes.summary: GradleRIO vendor dependency descriptor pulling in PhotonLib v2026.3.3 (photonlib and photontargeting, Java/JNI/C++) for PhotonVision-based coprocessor vision and AprilTag pose estimation.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Ignore-pattern list for the understand-anything analysis tool; gitignore-style globs (mostly commented-out suggestions) that exclude build artifacts and generated files from the knowledge-graph scan.

nodes.name: gradle-wrapper.properties

layers.name: Shared Library (frc.lib)
layers.description: Reusable, robot-agnostic building blocks — the LynkMotor/LynkSubsystem hardware-wrapper base classes, swerve module math and constants, unit conversions, hysteresis filtering, calibration lookup tables, and DogLog/Elastic logging helpers — plus the one unit test covering CalibrationTable.

layers.name: Subsystems
layers.description: The Climber, Feeder, Intake, Shooter, Controls, Detection, Pose, Swerve/SwerveAlign, LED, and Vision subsystems (each paired with its Constants file), which wrap CTRE hardware directly through LynkMotor rather than through a separate IO-interface/IOReal/IOSim split — this is the most densely interconnected group in the codebase.

layers.name: Coordination & Orchestration
layers.description: Superstructure, Aiming, and Shift — the layer that arbitrates and sequences multi-subsystem behavior (aiming solutions, alliance/practice-mode shifts) above the level of any single subsystem.

layers.name: Robot Core & Wiring
layers.description: The top-level robot entry point and global wiring — Main, Robot, Constants, Ports, CTREConfigs, Field, and FieldConstants — that instantiates subsystems and defines the port map, CAN/CTRE bus configuration, and field geometry shared across the project.

layers.name: Commands
layers.description: Command-based control behaviors layered on top of subsystems, including teleop swerve driving, aim-only assist, and the PID-driven swerve-to-object alignment routines under commands/pidswerve.

layers.name: Autonomous & Field Data
layers.description: Autonomous routine selection code (Autos, AutoConstants) together with the PathPlanner auto/path trajectory files, navgrid, and AprilTag field-layout JSONs (AndyMark and welded variants) that drive autonomous motion planning.

layers.name: Dashboard & Telemetry Config
layers.description: Driver-station and dashboard configuration — AdvantageScope layout, Elastic dashboard layout, and the deploy-side config/example files used for in-match telemetry and tuning.

layers.name: Build & Tooling
layers.description: Gradle build scripts and wrapper, WPILib project preferences, vendor dependency manifests (DogLog, PathplannerLib, Phoenix 6, WPILib New Commands, PhotonLib), the WPILib license, and the code-analysis ignore file that govern how the project builds and deploys rather than how the robot behaves.

tour.title: Robot Bootstrap: Main and Robot
tour.description: There is no README in this project, so the tour starts where the JVM starts. Main.java is the WPILib-mandated entry point — by convention it is kept intentionally empty, doing nothing but handing control to RobotBase.startRobot(Robot::new). Robot.java is where the real bootstrap happens: it extends TimedRobot, wires up DogLog telemetry and the WebServer, constructs every subsystem singleton (Swerve, Pose, Shooter, Feeder, Vision, LED, Controls, Superstructure), and dispatches the periodic/mode-transition callbacks that drive disabled, autonomous, teleop, and test modes. Everything else in this tour is something Robot.java pulls together.
tour.languageLesson: WPILib's Main/Robot split is a fixed framework convention, not a design choice this team made: Main.java must stay a trivial hand-off so the TimedRobot lifecycle (robotInit/robotPeriodic/autonomousInit/teleopPeriodic/...) is the only place initialization logic runs.

tour.title: Global Wiring: Ports and Constants
tour.description: Ports.java and Constants.java are the two most widely depended-upon files in the codebase (highest fan-in of any file, tied with Pose.java and Swerve.java) — nearly every subsystem reads from them. Ports.java is a central registry pairing every CAN device ID with its CAN bus, so a motor's physical wiring lives in exactly one place. Constants.java holds the driver-station flags, joystick deadband/sensitivity tuning, and shared timing thresholds referenced across mechanisms. Understanding these two files early explains a huge share of the cross-references you will see in every subsystem that follows.

tour.title: The LynkMotor / LynkSubsystem Pattern
tour.description: This is the core reusable abstraction the team built, and it defines this codebase's overall architecture: instead of a separate IO-interface / IOReal / IOSim split, every subsystem extends LynkSubsystem and talks to hardware through LynkMotor. LynkMotor wraps a CTRE TalonFX with stall detection, a homing/zeroing sequence, and config application, keeping raw Phoenix 6 calls out of subsystem logic. LynkSubsystem is the base class every subsystem extends, centralizing motor registration plus per-motor and global current/telemetry logging inside periodic() so no subsystem has to reimplement it. Every subsystem you see from here on is built on top of these two files.
tour.languageLesson: This is a composition-based hardware wrapper rather than the interface-based IO-isolation pattern (IOReal/IOSim per subsystem) used elsewhere — it trades simulation-swap flexibility for a single shared base class doing stall detection, homing, and telemetry logging once.

tour.title: Calibration Lookup Tables
tour.description: CalibrationTable.java is a generic linear-interpolation lookup table: given a scalar index like shot distance, it interpolates between the two nearest calibrated entries to produce a typed setpoint. Interpolatable.java is the single-method interface any setpoint type implements so the table knows how to blend two instances. This pattern is the shared-library building block the Shooter subsystem (next step) uses to convert distance into RPM and hood angle, and it is the one piece of this codebase with a dedicated unit test, confirming exact-match lookups, interpolation, and out-of-range handling all behave correctly.
tour.languageLesson: Interpolatable<T> is a small generic contract — CalibrationTable<T extends Interpolatable<T>> can interpolate between any calibration point type without knowing its concrete fields, as long as that type can blend itself against a neighbor.

tour.title: A Full Subsystem: Shooter
tour.description: Shooter.java is the clearest example of the LynkMotor/LynkSubsystem pattern applied end to end: it manages four flywheel motors (one leader, three followers) built through LynkMotor, extends LynkSubsystem for shared telemetry, and uses a CalibrationTable (from Step 4) to look up distance-based shoot and pass setpoints, plus a distance-to-time-of-flight table for shot timing. ShooterConstants.java defines the gearing, spin-up timing thresholds, and builds the flywheel/kicker MotorConfig objects the subsystem constructs from. Together they show how the abstractions from Steps 2-4 compose into a real, calibrated mechanism.

tour.title: Pose Estimation
tour.description: Pose.java is the singleton that owns the Pigeon2 gyro and the SwerveDrivePoseEstimator, fusing wheel odometry with vision measurements into a single field-relative pose. It also configures PathPlanner's AutoBuilder and derives higher-level field concepts other subsystems depend on directly — hub distance/bearing, alliance-flipped zones, trench-crossing status, and tilt/level detection. PoseConstants.java holds the gyro mount orientation and the robot's frame/bumper dimensions used to compute field boundaries. This is the highest fan-in code file in the project alongside Swerve and Constants, because nearly everything that needs to know 'where is the robot' — aiming, autos, LED warnings — reads from here.

tour.title: The Drivetrain: Swerve and SwerveModule
tour.description: Swerve.java owns the four SwerveModule instances and exposes field/robot-relative drive methods, an X-lock stance, brake/coast control, and SysId characterization routines. Notice the architectural contrast with Steps 3-5: SwerveModule.java wraps its CTRE TalonFX drive/angle motors and CANcoder directly rather than going through LynkMotor — a deliberate exception for the drivetrain's tight, latency-sensitive control loop. SwerveConstants.java is the single source of truth every swerve-related file reads from: module hardware selection, kinematics, gear ratios, PID/feedforward gains, and max speed.

tour.title: Aiming Geometry
tour.description: Aiming.java is a static utility class centralizing the robot's shot-aiming geometry: it computes shoot-on-the-move virtual targets (predicting flight time and robot movement to find where to actually aim), hub/pass alignment tolerances, and the automatic aiming rotation. It sits above Pose (Step 6) and Shooter (Step 5), consuming the pose estimate and shot-timing data from both to produce the rotation setpoint that both the shooter and the drivetrain's teleop driving code consume. This is the geometric brain that makes shoot-on-the-move possible.
tour.languageLesson: getVirtualTarget implements an iterative convergence loop — because the flight time depends on distance, and distance depends on the virtual target, and the virtual target depends on flight time, it re-solves the geometry a few times until the aim point stabilizes rather than computing it in one closed-form pass.

tour.title: Superstructure: Command-Factory Coordination
tour.description: Superstructure.java composes Shooter, Intake, Feeder, and Vision into higher-level scoring behaviors — DeliverToHub, Pass, FixedDelivery, SmartShoot, Unjam — and periodically tracks match-shift timing to drive dashboard telemetry, driver rumble, and LED warnings. Notice what this is NOT: unlike a SuperstructureState-enum-driven periodic() switch-case that centrally arbitrates state, Superstructure here is a command factory — it builds and returns composed Command objects from subsystem method calls, and WPILib's CommandScheduler does the actual arbitration by requiring exclusive subsystem ownership. This is a materially different coordination pattern worth contrasting against a state-machine Superstructure.

tour.title: Controls: The Input-to-Command Switchboard
tour.description: Controls.java is the singleton that owns the driver Xbox controller and wires every button, trigger, and POV binding to a command — swerve driving, Superstructure's scoring commands from Step 9, shooter/feeder/intake actions, and SysId diagnostic routines. With the highest fan-out of any subsystem file, it is the single place where you can see how every mechanism explained so far actually gets triggered by a human driver, tying the whole subsystem layer together into the robot's actual teleop behavior.

tour.title: Autonomous: PathPlanner Integration
tour.description: Autos.java is the highest fan-out file in the project: it integrates PathPlanner's AutoBuilder to dynamically construct scoring/intake auto sequences from dashboard chooser selections, provides path-shortening and mirroring modifiers, and tracks autonomous pose-drift error each cycle — reusing Pose (Step 6) for localization. AutoConstants.java holds the tuning tolerances and the PathPlanner RobotConfig built from SwerveConstants and motor specs. settings.json is PathPlanner's own project configuration — robot footprint, kinematics, mass/MOI/wheel-COF, and default motion constraints — that the code in Autos.java and Pose.java is built against; the .path file is one concrete recorded trajectory PathPlanner replays during a match.
tour.languageLesson: PathPlanner separates authoring from code: .path files are trajectories drawn in the PathPlanner GUI and deployed as data, while Autos.java only selects, sequences, and parameterizes them at runtime rather than encoding trajectory points directly in Java.

tour.title: Build and Vendor Tooling
tour.description: build.gradle is the capstone of the tour: it wires up the GradleRIO and Lombok plugins on a Java 17 toolchain, defines the RoboRIO deploy target, and declares every vendor dependency this codebase relies on — including a custom writeGitInfo task that stamps a git-describe version string into the deploy directory on every build. The Phoenix 6 vendordep is what makes LynkMotor and SwerveModule's TalonFX/CANcoder/Pigeon2 calls possible (Steps 3, 6-7); the PathplannerLib vendordep is what makes Autos.java's AutoBuilder integration (Step 11) possible. This is the layer that turns all the Java you have seen into a deployable RoboRIO artifact.
tour.languageLesson: GradleRIO vendordeps are JSON manifests, not Maven coordinates typed by hand — each one declares the Java/JNI/C++ artifact URLs for a vendor library (CTRE, PathPlanner) and build.gradle's WPILib plugin resolves them automatically, which is why adding a new vendor library means dropping a JSON file into vendordeps/ rather than editing the build script.
